headline: Wizards of the Coast strength lifts Hasbro; guidance raised
summary_short: Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $1.29B (+13.8% y/y per SEC-verbatim shard data), while GAAP diluted EPS fell to $1.12 (-19.4% q/q) on a $56M digital-games impairment and lingering costs from the previously disclosed network breach; management nonetheless raised full-year 2026 revenue, margin, and EBITDA guidance.
summary_long: Revenue grew 13.8% y/y to $1.29B, led by Wizards and Digital Gaming (+27% per the release, driven by Magic: The Gathering's first $500M quarter) and Consumer Products (+5%), partially offset by a 20% Entertainment decline. GAAP operating profit slipped 6.6% q/q to $252.5M and diluted EPS fell to $1.12, largely reflecting a $56M impairment on the Digital Games portfolio and $11M of incremental costs from the previously disclosed unauthorized network access (an estimated $25M revenue drag). Cash rose to $880.5M and long-term debt fell to $3.04B after $55M of debt paydown. Management raised FY2026 guidance: revenue growth to 5-7% constant currency (from 3-5%), adjusted operating margin to 25-26% (from 24-25%), and adjusted EBITDA to $1.45-1.50B (from $1.40-1.45B).

drivers.explanation: Growth led by Wizards and Digital Gaming (+27%, Magic: The Gathering's first $500M quarter) and Consumer Products (+5%), partially offset by a 20% Entertainment decline tied to deal timing.

Sequential decline reflects a $56M non-cash impairment on the Digital Games portfolio and $11M of incremental unauthorized-network-access costs; Wizards segment operating profit still rose 12% y/y on scale and mix.
Sequential fall driven by the Digital Games impairment and network-access costs; adjusted diluted EPS of $1.28 excludes those and other non-GAAP items.
Six-month operating cash flow of $604.4M drove the cash build, aided by $399.4M of new note proceeds partly used to reduce other borrowings.
Company raised FY2026 revenue, adjusted operating margin, and adjusted EBITDA guidance on broad-based strength, while continuing debt paydown and leaning into its $1B share-repurchase authorization.
